obligations.label: Subprocessor Authorization
obligations.quote: engage sub-processors at its own discretion

risk.rationale: high — Art. 28(3)(d) and Art. 28(2) require the controller's prior specific or general written authorisation. The clause appoints sub-processors at the processor's discretion and has the controller waive its right to object, which removes the authorisation entirely rather than channelling it.

obligations.label: Personal data breach notification
obligations.description: Art. 28(3)(f) GDPR: assist the controller with notification of a personal data breach.
obligations.quote: notify the Controller of a personal data breach

risk.rationale: CARRIED OVER FROM THE COMPOSITE v1 CLAUSE dpa.breach_and_dpia_assistance. Severity for this atomic duty is NOT yet calibrated separately and must be adjudicated. Original note: medium — Art. 28(3)(f) and Art. 33(2) require notification without undue delay. A fourteen day window is materially worse than the controller's own 72 hour obligation can absorb and should be negotiated, but a reviewer who accepted it with reasons would not be negligent.

obligations.label: Deletion Return
obligations.quote:
retain personal data
for its own legitimate business purposes

risk.rationale: high — Art. 28(3)(g) requires deletion or return at the controller's choice at the end of the services. Indefinite retention for the processor's own purposes, including model training, converts the processor into a controller for that processing without a lawful basis.

obligations.label: Audit Rights
obligations.quote:
On-site inspections and audits by the
Controller

risk.rationale: high — Art. 28(3)(h) requires the processor to allow for and contribute to audits, including inspections, conducted by the controller or a mandated auditor. Certification-first audit regimes are ordinary market practice and would be medium; this clause expressly excludes inspections, which removes a mandatory element rather than channelling it.

obligations.label: International Transfers
obligations.quote: transfer personal data to its affiliates in third countries

risk.rationale: high — Chapter V requires an adequacy decision or an Art. 46 safeguard to be in place before a transfer occurs. Permitting transfers now and addressing the mechanism 'if and when the need arises' inverts that sequence.
